summary: Working in linguistics and other fields, Furnivall studied at University College London and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He co-founded and taught at the Working Men's College, served as Secretary of the Philological Society (1853–1910), and was an Honorary Fellow at Trinity Hall.
Frederick M. Asher worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He spent his career at the University of Minnesota from circa 1971 to 2021, where he served as Professor from circa 1980 until 2021.

Working in Indology and religious studies, Smith was a student of Ludo Rocher. He held posts at the University of Iowa as Professor (attested 2006–2008) and later as Professor Emeritus (attested 2026).

Thomas was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at King Edward's School, Trinity College, Cambridge, and under Edward Byles Cowell. He served at the India Office Library (1898–1927) and as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1927–1937).

Bosch worked in Indology and archaeology after studying under Jacob Samuel Speyer and Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck. He headed the Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies (~1916–1936) and held professorships at Utrecht University (1938–1945) and Leiden University (1946–1957).

Barth studied at the University of Chicago and Cambridge under Edmund Ronald Leach. He held professorships at the University of Bergen (1961–1972), University of Oslo (1974), Emory University (1989–1996), Harvard (~1989–1996), and Boston University (~1997–2008).

Assandri works in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Heidelberg University under Rudolf G. Wagner, Günther Debon, and Günther-Dietz Sontheimer, and held an attested post at Heidelberg University in 2013.

Hardy was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Cologne and the University of Oxford, and held posts as Professor of Indian Religions at King's College London (~1974–2004) and Wilde Lecturer at Oxford (1985–1987).

Bischoff was a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Paris, Peking University, Hamburg, and the Mongolian Academy of Sciences, working under Marcelle Lalou and Robert des Rotours. He held professorships at Indiana (1964–1982), Hamburg (1982–1993), and Vienna (~1992–2009).

Rosen was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Franz Bopp. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at University College London (1828–1831) and Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London (1834).

Ukert was a scholar in the field of history and archaeology. He pursued his studies at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1798 to 1800 and at the University of Jena from circa 1800 to 1801.

Wolf worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne (~1777–1779) and held a post at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1783 to 1806.

Bechtel worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Heidelberg and Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and August Fick. He served as a Dozent at Göttingen (1884) and became Ordinarius in comparative linguistics at Halle-Wittenberg in 1895.

Bollensen, an Indologist, studied theology and Sanskrit at Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald (~1828–1832). He held teaching posts at the Gatchina Orphanage Institute, Saint Petersburg State University (~1844–1851), the Main Pedagogical Institute, and Kazan Federal University (1852–1856).
Brockhaus held posts as a professor at the University of Basel (~1871–1872), University of Jena (~1872–1877), University of Marburg (~1877–1888), and Kiel University (~1888–1895).

Andreas was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1868–1870) and held posts at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1887–1889) and the University of Göttingen (~1903–1930).
Diez was a linguist who studied at the universities of Giessen and Göttingen, and under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker. He held an academic post at the University of Bonn from circa 1823 to 1876.

Creuzer was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied at Tübingen and Jena, and held posts at Marburg (~1800–1804), Leiden (1809), and Heidelberg (~1804–1845).

Delitzsch worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Fleischer, Curtius, Windisch, Brockhaus, and Dillmann. He later held academic posts at the University of Breslau (~1893–1899) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1899–1920).
Krause was a Sinologist who studied at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen from circa 1904 to 1906. He later held an academic post at Heidelberg University from circa 1922 to 1935.
